newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Chechnya dialogue expected on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Chechnya dialogue expected on Saturday.

text.p: A postponed meeting aimed at paving the way for talks between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and leader of separatist Chechnya Aslan Maskhadov is likely to take place on Saturday, Kremlin officials said on Thursday.

A spokesman for Russia's powerful Security Council told Reuters its secretary, Ivan Rybkin, and Chechen First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov would meet and decide when the Yeltsin-Maskhadov talks would take place.
"The date of the talks will be decided during the meeting and announced after it," the spokesman said. "The two men are likely to meet on Saturday."

Udugov had been due to fly to Moscow on Thursday, but the meeting was postponed on Wednesday as tensions rose between Moscow and the separatist region after an incident earlier on Wednesday angily condemned by Udugov as "provocation".
Kremlin denied the situation had worsened and said the decision to put off the meeting was not directly linked to the incident.

Udugov said Russian fighter planes simulated an attack on the central market and airport in Grozny, the Chechen capital. Russia's military denied this, and sources in Chechnya's Interior Ministry identified the plane as actually Chechen.
Yeltsin on Wednesday reaffirmed his wish to meet Maskhadov in the near future but no date or venue was announced.

Talks aimed at normalising relations are stalled over the vexed issue of Chechnya's status, left unresolved when Russia withdrew its troops after signing a peace pact with Chehcnya, eneiding 21 months of bitter war.
Maskhadov, buoyed by the separatists' battlefield victory, insists that his republic is fully independent but Yeltsin wants Chechnya to remain loosely within the Russian Federation.
He said on Thursday he would insist on Chechnya's independence during talks with Yeltsin.
"Our position is... that the Chechen people has earned the right to be independent," Interfax quoted Maskhadov as saying.
But many analysts expect him to be much more flexible in the Russian capital than at home, where he faces many influential hardline nationalists.
